name: FAQ and Knowledge Base Calls
h1: Answer Repeat Questions by Phone From Your Own Knowledge Base
metaDescription: Teach a Calldesk agent your hours, policies and prices from your site or a Q&A list, and let it answer repeat questions while staff focus elsewhere.
intro: Look at a week of your incoming calls and a handful of questions will account for a large share of them: where are you, when do you close, do you take walk-ins, what does it cost to start, how do I return something. Each is a thirty-second answer, but thirty seconds multiplied across a week is hours of attention taken from work that needs a person. The risk with automating these answers is invention, a confident statement about a refund window nobody ever approved. A knowledge base keeps the agent anchored. In Calldesk you create a knowledge base for the agent from a website address, a PDF or manually entered question and answer pairs, and a knowledge-base step answers from that material. The faq-voice-agent template goes further and answers strictly from an approved FAQ, then escalates anything outside scope. The discipline is in the writing: short, direct answers in the words your staff would use, dated where policies change, and an explicit instruction to take a message when the answer is not there. Over time the call transcripts show which questions are unanswered, and each one is a new entry. Your team gets back the repetitive calls and keeps the unusual ones.
steps: Pull the twenty or so questions your team answers most often from email, voicemail and staff memory, and write each answer in two or three plain sentences.

Create a knowledge base with the agent's id set, since a knowledge-base step sees just content attached to its own agent. Use manual question and answer items, a website address or a PDF as the source.
Create an agent from the faq-voice-agent template and point its knowledge-base step at your content.
Write the out-of-scope rule explicitly: when the answer is not in the knowledge base, the agent says so, takes a name and number, and does not guess.
Add a transfer step for callers who ask for a person, with an hours check if staff are not always available.
Publish, route a number, and place test calls using the odd phrasings real callers use, not just your written questions.
Each week, read transcripts for unanswered questions and add them as new knowledge items.

sampleCallFlow.speaker: agent
sampleCallFlow.text: Thanks for calling Fernhill Community Pool. I'm an AI assistant and I can answer questions about hours, fees and classes. What would you like to know?

sampleCallFlow.speaker: caller
sampleCallFlow.text: Do you have lap swim early in the morning?

sampleCallFlow.speaker: agent
sampleCallFlow.text: Yes, lap swim runs from six to eight on weekdays. Drop-in is available without a booking.

sampleCallFlow.speaker: agent
sampleCallFlow.text: A single drop-in adult swim is on our fees page at eight dollars.

sampleCallFlow.speaker: caller
sampleCallFlow.text: And do you do swim lessons for a four year old?

sampleCallFlow.speaker: agent
sampleCallFlow.text: We run preschool lessons for ages three to five on Saturday mornings. I don't have the current waiting list information, though. Would you like me to take your name and number so staff can follow up?

sampleCallFlow.speaker: caller
sampleCallFlow.text: Yes please. It's Hannah, five five five, zero one six three.

sampleCallFlow.speaker: agent
sampleCallFlow.text: Thanks, Hannah. I've noted a question about preschool lesson availability. Someone will call you.

featuresUsed.howItHelps: Answers come from a knowledge base built from your website, a PDF or manual question and answer items.
The agent answers from that content automatically when a caller asks a question.
When an answer is missing, the caller's name, number and question are captured for staff.
A caller who wants a person can be passed to one, instead of being kept in the loop.
Transcripts show which questions callers ask and which the knowledge base failed to answer.

featuresUsed.feature: Call testing and simulation test cases
featuresUsed.howItHelps: You can try awkward phrasings before launch and rerun scenarios after editing the knowledge base.

considerations: The agent is as accurate as the material you give it. Date your policies and review the knowledge base whenever prices, hours or rules change.
Leave medical, legal and financial advice out of the knowledge base. The answer for those topics is a message or a transfer to a qualified person.
If the knowledge base is built from your website, check what the page text actually says, since old pages can contradict current policy.

faq.q: Where can the knowledge come from?
faq.a: A knowledge base can be created from a website address, a PDF or manually entered question and answer items, and the API accepts question and answer items directly.

faq.q: Why did my agent not use the knowledge base?
faq.a: A knowledge-base step sees just the content from a knowledge base attached to its own agent, so create the knowledge base with that agent's id.

faq.q: What does it do when it does not know?
faq.a: That is controlled by your instructions. We recommend telling it to say it does not have the answer and to take a message or transfer the call.

faq.q: Is the answer read word for word?
faq.a: The agent uses the entries to answer in conversation, so wording can vary. Where exact wording matters, put it in a fixed spoken line in the flow.

faq.q: How often should I update it?
faq.a: Whenever the underlying fact changes, and as a habit after reviewing a week of transcripts for questions the knowledge base missed.
